sources.entry: geoai-skills by muend - Skills for geospatial analysis that require coordinate-system, spatial-validation and comparability checks before a result is reported, and narrow or refuse a claim the data cannot support. Ships a paired evaluation against a skills-disabled control arm.

summary.one_liner: A set of 18 vendor-neutral Agent Skills that make coding agents check coordinate systems, comparability, leakage, and uncertainty before reporting a geospatial result, and narrow or refuse claims the data cannot support.
summary.what_it_does: The repository provides 18 narrow Agent Skills covering geospatial work such as remote sensing, change detection, point-cloud/LiDAR, terrain hydrology, spatial statistics, geostatistics, MCDA suitability, network accessibility, PostGIS SQL, Google Earth Engine, cartography, and gated ArcGIS Pro automation. Each skill is meant to be routed by its domain and to enforce preconditions like CRS selection, unit verification, validity checks, spatial (blocked) validation, and provenance. When evidence is insufficient, the skills direct the agent to produce a narrower claim, a clarification request, a provisional plan, or a refusal. The README reports a routing benchmark (167 cases) and a paired behavior evaluation (92 clean pairs, skills enabled vs. disabled on one Claude Code/model pair), and states that the behavior run failed its own quality gate. It also describes a separately reported external transfer subset of 5 cases. The skills are packaged for Codex, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, the Skills CLI, ChatGPT, and Claude.ai ZIP upload.
use_cases: Checking whether two satellite scenes support a changed-area claim
Auditing spatial validation for geospatial machine learning models
Selecting projected CRS and verifying units for area or distance measurement
Reviewing PostGIS spatial SQL for correctness and index use
Validating AHP weights and suitability mapping workflows
Gating destructive local ArcGIS Pro edits
how_to_run: npx skills add muend/geoai-skills --skill remote-sensing-analysis -a claude-code
stack: ArcGIS Pro (optional, Windows only, via arcgis-mcp-bridge)
Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot plugin/skill formats
notable: Emphasizes refusing or narrowing claims when data cannot support them, rather than producing invented certainty
Publishes a paired skills-enabled vs. control behavior evaluation and openly reports the failed quality gate
Separates routing benchmark, behavior measurement, and external transfer evidence instead of pooling them
Explicitly positions itself as a method/verification layer that complements GDAL, PostGIS, QGIS, ArcGIS, and similar tools
Vendor-neutral, with install paths for multiple agent surfaces
caveats: The README states the absolute quality level is not good enough: only 18/92 behavior cases met every criterion and the critical-failure rate was 4.3%, failing the repository's Phase 3 gate.
Behavior results are single model-judged, uncalibrated, not yet human-verified, and tied to one runtime/model pair; the README says they are not universal claims.
Real ArcGIS Pro execution requires Windows, licensed ArcGIS Pro, and a configured local arcgis-mcp-bridge.
